microtheory.name: performance_arts
microtheory.definition: Theater, drama, dance, performance theory. Aristotelian Poetics, Stanislavski's method, Brecht's distancing effect (Verfremdungseffekt), Grotowski's poor theater, Boal's theater of the oppressed, performance studies (Schechner). Live performance as a discipline distinct from music + literature + film. Substrate analogue: substrate's enacted-vs-described modes.

concepts.name: theater
concepts.definition: Live performance involving actors enacting a story for audience. Greek origin: theatron = 'seeing place'. Substrate analogue: enacted substrate-state for an audience.

concepts.name: drama
concepts.definition: Literary genre intended for performance. Aristotle's three unities (action, time, place). Substrate analogue: substrate's narrative-form output.

concepts.name: tragedy
concepts.definition: Aristotle: serious action, complete, with magnitude. Protagonist with fatal flaw (hamartia). Catharsis through pity + fear. Substrate analogue: substrate's failure-mode-as-narrative.

concepts.name: comedy
concepts.definition: Aristotle: imitation of inferior characters; ends in restoration. Substrate analogue: substrate's correction-arrives-in-time.

concepts.name: dance
concepts.definition: Patterned body movement as art. Choreography + improvisation. Folk, classical, modern, contemporary, postmodern.

concepts.name: opera
concepts.definition: Sung drama. Italian invention ~1600. Wagner's Gesamtkunstwerk total art work.

concepts.name: aristotle_poetics
concepts.definition: Aristotle's 'Poetics' (~335 BCE). Founding document of dramatic theory. Plot, character, thought, diction, melody, spectacle as elements of tragedy. Catharsis. Substrate analogue: substrate's narrative-element ontology.

concepts.name: stanislavski_method
concepts.definition: Konstantin Stanislavski 1900s. Actor's psychological technique: emotional memory, given circumstances, magic if, super-objective. Foundation of method acting (Strasberg, Adler, Meisner).

concepts.name: brechts_verfremdung
concepts.definition: Bertolt Brecht. Distancing effect — make familiar strange so audience thinks critically rather than empathises uncritically. Epic theater. Substrate analogue: substrate's reflective distance from object-level state.

concepts.name: grotowski_poor_theater
concepts.definition: Jerzy Grotowski. Strip theater to actor-audience encounter; reject scenic apparatus. Body as primary instrument.

concepts.name: boal_theatre_of_oppressed
concepts.definition: Augusto Boal 1970s. Forum theater. Spectators become spect-actors, intervening in scenes about oppression. Theater as rehearsal for revolution.

concepts.name: performance_studies
concepts.definition: Richard Schechner 1980s. Performance as broad category: theater + ritual + sport + everyday performance. Performativity (Butler).

concepts.name: performativity_butler
concepts.definition: Judith Butler 1990. Gender + identity constituted by reiterated performative acts, not pre-existing essences. Substrate analogue: substrate's identity-by-repeated-act.

concepts.name: scene
concepts.definition: Continuous action in single location + time. Substrate analogue: substrate's atomic narrative unit.

concepts.name: act_dramatic
concepts.definition: Major division of play, often corresponding to dramatic arc segment. Five-act (Shakespeare), three-act (modern).

concepts.name: monologue
concepts.definition: Long speech by single character. Internal or addressed. Hamlet's soliloquies.

concepts.name: dialogue_theater
concepts.definition: Exchange between characters. Vehicle of dramatic action.

concepts.name: fourth_wall
concepts.definition: Imaginary boundary between performers + audience. Realist theater. Brecht broke it; immersive theater (Punchdrunk) erases it.

concepts.name: suspension_of_disbelief
concepts.definition: Coleridge. Audience accepts fictional premises for sake of engagement. Substrate analogue: substrate's bracketing of frame disagreement.

concepts.name: mise_en_scene
concepts.definition: Total visual composition of staged scene. Lighting, set, costume, blocking.

concepts.name: blocking
concepts.definition: Choreography of actors' positions + movements on stage.

concepts.name: improv_theater
concepts.definition: Unscripted performance. Spolin + Johnstone foundational. 'Yes, and...' principle. Substrate analogue: substrate's exploratory generation under acceptance rules.

concepts.name: method_acting
concepts.definition: Lee Strasberg's adaptation of Stanislavski. Affective memory. De Niro, Day-Lewis.

concepts.name: physical_theater
concepts.definition: Body-primary tradition. Lecoq, Decroux, Pina Bausch's Tanztheater. Movement as language.

concepts.name: ritual_performance
concepts.definition: Schechner: performance-as-ritual + ritual-as-performance. Religious ceremony, sports, parade all enact something. Substrate analogue: substrate's repeated structural enactment.

concepts.name: embodied_practice
concepts.definition: Knowledge held in trained body — actor's instinct, dancer's musculature. Cannot be fully verbalised. Substrate analogue: substrate's procedural-Mt knowledge.

rules.name: catharsis_via_pity_and_fear
rules.head: Jabberwock considers tragedy's effect
rules.body: Aristotle: through arousing + then releasing pity + fear, tragedy purges (catharsis) the audience. Substrate's emotion-resolution mechanism.

rules.name: performance_is_enacted_not_described
rules.head: Jabberwock distinguishes performance from literature
rules.body: performance lives in present-tense bodily enactment; literature lives in textual description. Different medium, different epistemology. Substrate's enacted-vs-described distinction.

rules.name: distancing_enables_critical_engagement
rules.head: Jabberwock wants audience to think rather than just feel
rules.body: Brechtian distancing (Verfremdung) — break empathic immersion, foreground constructedness. Substrate's reflective-meta vs immersive-object mode.

rules.name: performativity_constitutes_identity_through_repetition
rules.head: Jabberwock considers identity formation
rules.body: Butler: gender + identity are reiterated performative acts that constitute (not express) the self. Substrate's repeated-enactment-as-identity.

rules.name: embodied_knowledge_resists_verbalisation
rules.head: Jabberwock has knowledge held in procedural form
rules.body: trained-body knowledge (actor's instinct, dancer's musculature) cannot be fully verbalised. Procedural is not declarative. Substrate's procedural-Mt limit.
